transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: S-Net broadband diagnostics, Kieran speaking. What is the issue with your service today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Kieran. Our fiber broadband has been dropping twenty times a day for three solid weeks, and every time I ring up your call center, your agents tell me that if an engineer visits and doesn't find a street fault, I will be slapped with a one hundred and twenty pound callout fee! I have lost three weeks of remote work pay as an independent accountant because my secure VPN drops out!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What exact color is the broadband internet indicator light on your front router panel when the disconnect occurs?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The internet light flashes amber for two minutes, turns solid red, and then slowly cycles back to flashing white before reconnecting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the optical line interface status on your terminal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My mobile contact number is zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero seven two five, and we are currently on the Gigafast 500 package with an optical ONT on our hallway wall.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm the technical symptoms: your broadband experiences intermittent drops multiple times daily with an amber and red LED cycle, and you are seeking an engineer visit without incurring callout penalty fees. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly that. It dropped right in the middle of a crucial HMRC client tax audit submission this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are these drops occurring at specific regular intervals or randomly throughout the day and evening?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: They occur completely randomly, sometimes twice an hour, sometimes five times in an afternoon, making it impossible to hold Zoom client consultations.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is the Hub router connected directly into the primary optical ONT unit using the supplied red Ethernet patch cable without passing through extension leads?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is connected with the original red Ethernet cable that Openreach supplied, plugged directly into LAN Port 1.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am going to trigger a comprehensive twenty-four hour line attenuation diagnostic test on your optical profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are you still there on the phone, Kieran?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, apologies for the pause. The optical line test shows forty-eight micro-dropouts registered over the past seventy-two hours on the Cambridge exchange concentrator.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Forty-eight dropouts in three days! That proves beyond any shadow of a doubt that the fault is outside my house on the physical street line!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Intermittent micro-dropouts can originate from either external distribution fiber splices or internal optical patch leads inside the premises.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So will you finally dispatch an engineer without threatening me with that ridiculous one hundred and twenty pound penalty fee?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Company policy strictly dictates that any engineer visit requires customer pre-authorization for potential sixty-five or one hundred and twenty pound equipment charges if internal customer equipment is faulty.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why should I pre-authorize an extortionate charge when your own computer system just proved there were forty-eight drops on your network?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If the field technician determines the fault is on our network side, the fee is automatically waived.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you guarantee in writing that the fee will be waived?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the Openreach engineer availability schedule for your postcode area.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello, Kieran, is the system still searching?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, apologies. The earliest available Openreach optical engineer appointment is tomorrow morning between eight and one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning works for me, I will make sure I am home.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have booked the engineer appointment and noted on the ticket that external optical attenuation was detected.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the technician have access to the street cabinet if the underground fiber splice is degraded or waterlogged?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, Openreach optical technicians carry optical time-domain reflectometers and fusion splicing equipment to test and repair external distribution nodes, underground footway boxes, and overhead manifolds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will hopefully resolve whatever physical fault is breaking down the street.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also applied an engineer fee waiver pre-authorization flag to the priority dispatch ticket under technical reference FLT-88201.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives me genuine reassurance that I won't get a surprise one hundred and twenty pound charge on my next monthly direct debit bill.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm what you mentioned earlier, your registered contact telephone number is zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero seven two five?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero seven two five.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have registered that mobile number for direct engineer arrival SMS tracking notifications with a thirty-minute warning window.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That way I will know when the technician is ten minutes away so I can let them through the front security gates.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Will the engineer require access to your rear garden or only the front hallway?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Only the front hallway right where the white optical ONT box is mounted on the wall above the power socket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That will keep the internal diagnostic testing fast and straightforward for the optical technician.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What should I do if the broadband drops again this evening before the engineer arrives tomorrow morning?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do not reboot the optical ONT tonight, as power cycling erases the diagnostic error counters that the engineer needs to inspect on their handheld testing meter.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will leave the power plugs and cables completely untouched overnight so the logs stay intact.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will also apply a twenty-pound goodwill credit to your broadband account to compensate for the three weeks of intermittent connection issues.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, that helps offset the mobile data charges I had to burn on my smartphone hotspot tethering.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: If that engineer fails to show up tomorrow after three weeks of misery, I swear I will cancel our direct debit, terminate the contract, and take S-Net straight to the communications ombudsman!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: All engineer visits booked through the priority gateway are subject to contractor availability and severe weather constraints.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You don't care at all about the immense disruption and lost income this has caused to my livelihood!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The appointment is confirmed in the national engineering dispatch database under priority tier two.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let's hope they actually arrive this time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will receive an automated text confirmation and tracking link within fifteen minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I will watch for that confirmation text.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your contract includes standard residential service level agreements for residential optical connections, ensuring priority dispatch on persistent micro-faults.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our download speeds are great when it works, we get five hundred megabits down and one hundred megabits up, so the speed is fine when connected.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The underlying gigabit optical capacity is very robust once the physical splice on the street distribution point is permanently repaired.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What is the appointment booking reference number for the engineer?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The booking reference number is ENG-44910-V.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Writing that booking reference down on my desk notepad... ENG-44910-V. I will have that ready for the Openreach engineer tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have verified that the priority Openreach optical engineer slot is booked for tomorrow morning between eight and one, the fee waiver pre-authorization flag is permanently locked on your docket, and the twenty-pound credit is applied. Does that address all your concerns today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, you've booked the engineer and waived the fee, which is what I needed. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today. Have a good afternoon. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Kieran, goodbye.
